turnaround_reason: Sarepta collapsed (~-86% over 12 months) after three patient deaths from acute liver failure tied to its AAVrh74 gene-therapy platform, an FDA request to suspend Elevidys distribution, clinical holds on multiple programs, and class-action suits. The 'basing' setup reflects a stock trying to find a floor amid an unresolved safety/regulatory crisis.
bullish_points: Off the 52-week low ($14.68 vs $18.39 spot); recent quarters beat EPS (Q2 +27.6%, Q1 +202%), and the exon-skipping (EXONDYS/VYONDYS/AMONDYS) franchise still generates ~$2B revenue
Forward P/E ~7.1 and P/B ~1.27 price in a lot of bad news; Roche/Arrowhead collaborations retain optionality
Any FDA resolution allowing Elevidys distribution to resume would be a sharp positive re-rate catalyst
Solid liquidity: $788M cash, current ratio 4.4 — not a near-term solvency risk
bearish_points: Core safety crisis is unresolved: 3 deaths, distribution suspension, and clinical holds across the AAVrh74 platform — an open-ended, potentially existential overhang
Revenue -34% YoY and gross margin -17% TTM; Elevidys (the growth engine) is effectively offline
Active class-action litigation adds legal/financial tail risk and management-credibility damage
Debt $1.06B > cash; 'hold' consensus with target dispersion from $5 to $38 signals genuine binary uncertainty
catalyst: FDA decision on resuming Elevidys distribution / lifting clinical holds; updated safety mitigation plan. Q3 earnings 2026-11-04 as a checkpoint.
catalyst_timing: FDA path is open-ended (no fixed date); next earnings 2026-11-04
suggested_trade: Pass / watchlist only. This is a falling-knife biotech with an unresolved, potentially existential safety-regulatory overhang. If any position, a tiny speculative call spread sized to lose 100% — not a spot commitment.
key_risk: The FDA does not permit Elevidys/AAVrh74 programs to resume (or another death occurs), permanently impairing the growth franchise and cratering the equity.
would_skip_if: No credible line of sight to distribution resumption, additional adverse safety events, or escalating litigation — i.e., the current base case, hence the low conviction.
